text: Horribly underrated game. The controls are a bit strange, but once you get past the initial learning curve, it's incredibly fun. Beautiful graphics even on a lower end system, visceral combat, interesting characters/classes. The story's also a lot better than you'd expect, though it may not seem that way at first. Gameplay's a bit of a departure from the previous installments in the series (to say the least), but most changes are for the better, and the story connects back to the first game's much better than DS2's did. My only major complaints are that the audio can be buggy at times, and some of the voice acting is what I will politely call less than stellar. But even with those issues, it's one of the best RPGs I've played in a long time.

text: Before I begin: My opinion on this game is actually neutral if it is leaning more towards the negativ than the positiv, just not enough to honestly justify a thumbs down. Now I, like many other fans of the series, was excited when I heard news about about a new DS and couldn't wait to play it. Sadly my enthusiasm was quickly destroyed by two things: 1. You can't create your own character, instead there are 4 you can choose from. 2. Those character have 2 styles each. Now for those who don't know what's so bad about it let me explain: In DS you could always create your main character, the companions however where pre-created obviously and your fighting-style as well as your skill were determined by your playstlye. This mean that if you continued to use a certain style your character would get better and better with it. And , at least in DS 1, the stats for that style would raise as well. Well in the end, after it was avaible for a few bucks, I decided to play it anyways and quite honestly was exactly what I suspected it to be if slightly worse in some aspects. Now first of the good things about it: +The combat all around seem more dynamic, while it was very possible to win with little to no movement in the first two games that would be a death ticket in this one. Some might hate it but I kind of like it even it it is sometimes kind of clumsy. +It looks good, well most of the time... and yes I know graphics are not everything. +The story CAN be interesting, or at least entertaining. Especially if you take a drink everytime someone says "Jeyne     Kassynder" in a dramatic fashion. Now it's weakpoints: -Those f*cking bosses, now don't get me wrong, I love a challenging boss like everyone else but if it's difficulty is purely based on it having ♥♥♥♥ton of HP as well as respawning minions? Not so much. There are bosses where it make sense (the warbeast comes to mind) but most of the time it fells more like the developers were lazy. -The characters are just stupid. No really they are. Imagine this: Your antagonist, who by the way controls the entire army of the church, wants every legionaire and anyone connected with the legion dead.... what do they do? RALLY ALL SURVIVORS IN THE ♥♥♥♥ING MANSION OF THE GRANDMASTER! Sure! It's not obvious or anything like that, not like Jeyne could have spies nearby or anything like that! The next destination after the obvious happens? THE LAST CHAPTERHOUSE! Are those guys ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥?! While I am at it: I really wish I could have told some of those guys to go screw themselves. -Those "triggered" fights, to summarize: You see an obvious foe; you attack; nothing happens. You go closer, a cutscene starts and BOOM! in the middle of an "ambush" or something similar. Not to bad with the melee-fighter but as a ranged one? -The desing on several character is just... ugh... really just uncomfortable. Old character sometimes look like albinos in their 30's and they will NEVER. STOP. MOVING. THEIR. EYES! Really ?! Look me in the eyes and not at the ceiling damn it! -It just didn't fell like a DS-game... instead it relied on references to older game while practically screaming that it's a DS aswell and we should notice it. -Square Enix In the end? Is the game good? No not really but it's also not horrible either instead it's in that weird limbo where some will like it while others despise it. Now if this games catches your fancy, buy it but wait for a sale. It can be fun but you won't miss anything. But if you really REALLY need to play it: Play as Anjali, makes for a better story.

text: One of the first games I've ever bought on Steam and to this day still one of my favorites. Why? The replay value, I never get tired of playing this one. There are several options you can tweak to alter your play style, the levels are all randomly generated, plus you can choose from a long list of "professions" to change your abilities/spells with each new try you make at beating the final floor. (or at least getting farther than you got last time) Depending on what you pick from the profession list, you can spend your time crafting plenty of neat things to help you hack and slash your way through the dungeon. Engineering is one of my favorites to have, (making bombs, chainsaws and armor that lets me survive being struck by lightning is always a plus). But there's much more to pick from than that, which always gives you something new to try each time you play. Want to make a Thief that knows Blacksmithing and can teleport? You can do that. How about a Pirate that makes acid potions you can throw on crowds of monsters but can also summon minnions to fight for you at will. Yeah, you can do that too. There are so many combinations to choose from, it keeps the game interesting for a really long time. So yes, I recommend this game. Not just for the all the movie and game references you can find on a lot of the items or all the random jibberish the monsters will say to you, but for the sheer amount of fun I have had wandering around the dungeon looking for treasure..and usually finding a Monster Zoo..(that's an entire room FILLED with monsters..yeah.)

title: dungeons of dredmor
text: The short version: It's fun.  Build character, collect loot, be a god on one floor and die to a piece of vegetable on the next. The long version: This game is a turn-based, dungeon crawling, rogue-like-power-fantasy. That last bit may sound contradictory but in the same game I slaughtered an entire room of 50 something+ monsters without batting an eye and ran like a baby carrot panda from a stupid corn thing. The character building is fantastic as the player can choose a handful of skill trees which creates a lot of different character builds. Progressing down different trees in different order can create a new experience for the playthrough. The rogue-like aspects are tweakable so the player can choose how difficult or easy a playthrough will be. They can even turn off perma-death and load a save when a character dies. Along with the built in options, this game is moddable with Steam Workshop support for easy browsing/installation. Combat is turn-based and depending on how you setup your character it can range from flinging fireballs and running away until things are recharged to teleporting into the thick of things and slowly laying the smack down on every living thing in the area. Crafting is a little clunky. It has a lot of depth and that can be a blessing and a curse. The player has a limited inventory space but the amount of crafting materials is a little overwhelming at first. In general, there is a crafting material for each craft (smithing, tinkering, etc) and for each crafting material there are multiple levels (copper, silver, brass, etc). Inventory can become cluttered unless the player is not a hoarder (what's wrong with you?) and they know exactly what they want to make and how much of a certain material is required. On the other hand, the depth allows for a lot of customization and there are even recipes to be found on bookshelves to create even more things. The humor and flavor text in the game is a bit of hit or miss. While it can be funny, at times it gets in the way of figuring out what exactly a skill does. This can also be half the fun for some. As for the story, something something evil something something you are the one panda to save them all. Yeah, game's about loot and poking things till they're puddles of goo. It's a great game for people who like to experiment with builds and go dungeon crawling/loot collecting through randomized levels. If you don't like the rogue-like element, you can turn it into a rogue-lite. Mods extend the fun.

text: This isn't a terrible game, so consider it a mixed review, but after 30 hours in and not wanting to play anymore and not very excited about it, I can't rate this positively for a rogue-like game.  I will note, though, that if you generially like the idea of "rogue-likes" but are mostly turned off by lack of feedback/graphics/music, this is a good game to get into the genre. Quick review: Pros: -Varied builds -Lots of loot -Very good music -Good graphics -Standard hard rogue difficulty curve -Cute mechanics like monster horde rooms Cons: -Very repetitive, imagine a single player only diablo -Catastrophically bad inventory management -Grindy as heck, even on the no grind game option (lol) -Not very well balanced -Surprisngly simple for a rogue game Details: Possibly the worst part of the game is the inventory management.  This sounds like a weird gripe, and I've played lots of games with terrible inventory management and just dealt with it, but this is definitely the worst inventory management in a game I've ever seen.  Basically you've got somewhere on the order of 1000 different item types in the game, and all can be used to craft stuff, but you can only hold onto 60ish items at a time.  Sure you have a dimensional stash that you can visit any time, but with that many item types, you'll be visiting it every 3 minutes. Even choosing a no-crafting skills build, which seems to be the only option, its still surprisingly annoying to deal with given you need food and booze of which there's like 100 types.  So then it comes down to choosing builds that don't craft and use vampirism (no food), and don't use throwing or crossbows,  just to play the game without going insane. Next up is the repetitiveness.  Most roguelikes have unique enemies with interesting abilities, enviromental hazards, and their own brew of general randomness to spice things up.  This game is mostly just stacking on various resistances and bonuses and dealing with your enemy's resistances and bonuses.  You look at the forums, and most build discussion is even just about choosing builds that let you stack certain stats.  This kind of munchkinery is super fun for about 15 hours or so, but it gets old really quick.  When you combine this with the fact that a floor takes about an hour (half an hour on "no grind" lol) and there's fifteen floors, and you're mostly just spamming the left mouse button, I think a lot of people will just get bored.  Even with the builds that implement some form of strategy, it's going to be the exact same strategy for any situation. There's some major balance concerns as well, although since it's single player, you can just opt out of using the overpowered crap or choose random builds.

text: 6/10 I'm so torn on this game. It's illustrated super well and the aesthetic is great. The combat is smooth and enjoyable. The music is nice. The main character is very well animated. However, there are issues that seem almost contradictory to the positives about the game. For example: -The combat is satisfying, and in that the counter/parry move is very satisfying to perform, but the timing for the counter is overly-strict and feels inconsistent with the enemy animations at times. -Another thing is, while the main character is very well animated, every other character and almost every creature looks like their animations are from a flash game (this isn't really visible in still screenshots). They look like they're just very obvious limbs with hinges at the elbows etc. Even the main character's animations turn HORRIBLE in the very last scene of the game. There was also the weird jarring fact that one character (just one, and not the main character either. a rather minor one) had a 3D model when he speaks in dialogue. Just some random cel shaded guy while everyone else is 2D... There's also, again, one single enemy type only at the end that is 3D, again it's just an insignificant enemy. -The art in the game is all very well drawn, but the character portraits in dialogue scenes are lower quality than the rest of the game's art, and also very obviously stretched bigger than they should be. -The story is decent and some voices are well done, but others are terrible and I can't stand the main character's voice or the way he talks. That, mixed with the terrible animations of everyone but Dust, really takes me out of the story constantly. -Secrets and puzzles are nice, but they seem overused here. I get that it's a metroid-vania, but you run past SO MANY things that you have to come back for later. It made it feel like padding out the game at some point. -Frankly I can't say that I have sufficient technical knowledge about this kind of thing to have authority, but there also were a lot of things that bugged me with the balance of the game. Some enemies felt like they hit too hard/had too much health compared to the player. The further you get into the game the more healing items felt way off when it comes to price/healing ratio. I believe the best healing item I saw was for 300hp, when I had 1800... On top of that, 300hp is like 1-2 hits from the higher enemies. And I probably could have bought like 25 of those tops if I had spent ALL of my money. Then at the same time there are certain items that feel super OP toward the end. My magic abilities went from low-damage but useful for crowd control, to by far my strongest attacks VERY quickly and suddenly toward the end. My "Fidget" stat went from around 250 to over 3800 in just the last couple hours of the game from some new items I got. And none of those items were things I had to grind for, while at the same time the last armor piece I saw was just an incremental upgrade from the previous one, but I would have had to grind just to get the materials to forge it. The whole item system seems off balance. I also never needed the vast majority of the materials and blueprints I picked up. Overall, I wish I could give it an "indifferent" rather than up or down. If you can look past those things, I'd recommend it, however I personally felt like I was having to force myself to keep going several times. I honestly can't even decide if I would say I enjoyed the game or not overall. It's just so jarring to have some aspects be really well done, but at the same time have those same aspects be done so poorly at the same time in other areas (e.g. animations, art, etc). Based on the fact that I don't think I would have played it if I had known how I'd feel about all these things from the start, I think I'm going to have to give it a pass.

text: Most of the reviews here have this game described fairly well. Dying Light is something of a mash up of Mirror's Edge and Dead Island, but considerably more fun to play than either. You end up with several offensive and defensive options to use against the neverending hoard of zombie and human opponents, and using these options feels fluid and fun to use. The environments are well done, and getting around seldom feels tedious. My only real criticism that I can see so far is how annoyingly bad the dialog/story can be at moments. The option to skip dialog/cutscenes as needed is a great feature, but some of the voice acting and dialog from side characters is enjoyable enough that I don't skip most things outside of the somewhat cringe-inducing main storyline. The drop-in/out co-op has made playing this with a friend exceedingly easy and the game doesn't do anything to complicate the enjoyment of the co-op experience. This is easily the most fun I've had playing co-op since Borderlands 2, and I feel the developer was taking the best possible notes from that series when they made Dying Light.

Trying to keep it together as a group when a hoard of virals are hot on your heals is both terrifying and hilarious at the same time, we ended up chased into an apartment complex which turned out to be a dead end. But thanks to great teamwork we actually held out till morning by holding a small apartment with one entrance, one person would heal and repair his weapons while lending an occasional kick while the two others held the Volatiles at bay with UV lights and everything from leg furniture to screwdrivers and wrenches. Most heart racing experience I have had in gaming for a very long-time, our elation at surviving however went south when we realised the battered and retreating Volatiles had been replaced by a hoard of zombies “biters” that swarmed the building we were in. Seeing your team being dragged down one at the time by a wall of dead flesh, before being pulled out of your corner and devoured was surprisingly enjoyable. Only real thing I can put my finger on is optimization, the game doesn’t seem to be 100% optimized and if you have AMD graphic card you might encounter some FPS drops that shouldn’t happen.
